articles.title: Pós-menopausa não é catástrofe, diz escritora Melanie Pérez Arias | G1
articles.standfirst: Em seu primeiro romance, a escritora venezuelana-peruana Melanie Pérez Arias usa a queda inexplicável de cabelo de uma mulher como ponto de partida para explorar identidade, perdas, corpo feminino e amizade.
articles.summary: A escritora Melanie Pérez Arias explora a pós-menopausa e o corpo feminino em um romance que transforma a perda de cabelo em uma jornada de amizade e libertação.
articles.body:
Un Animal que se Deja Caer é o primeiro romance da escritora venezuelano-peruana Melanie Pérez Arias. — Foto: Nolan Rada

Pense por apenas um segundo: o que significa o seu cabelo para você?

Se, algum dia, você o perdesse sem causa aparente , o que estaria disposta a oferecer ou ao que renunciaria para tê-lo de volta?

O cabelo, segundo a escritora venezuelana-peruana Melanie Pérez Arias, de 40 anos, é algo que não sangra, mas dói.

E, no seu primeiro romance Un Animal que se Deja Caer ( Um animal que se deixa cair , em tradução literal), o cabelo é o ponto de partida para toda uma viagem íntima sobre a identidade, perdas, renúncias e, sobretudo, a amizade no universo feminino.

A obra acompanha Miriam, a protagonista, em uma cidade e em paisagens cujos nomes não são identificados. A escolha busca dar universalidade à narrativa, para que qualquer pessoa possa se reconhecer nela: a história de um corpo que falha sem aviso, de um grupo de amigas que representa a família escolhida e dos silêncios, tabus e mitos que ainda cercam o corpo feminino.

Em um livro que é América Latina, mas sobretudo, Caribe (com sincretismo, humor em meio à tragédia e um certo toque de salsa), Pérez Arias também elabora uma magia narrativa, evitando que a história que ela conta toque o presente do seu país de nascimento. E esta, segundo ela, é uma decisão política.

A BBC News Mundo, o serviço em espanhol da BBC, conversou com Melanie Pérez Arias durante o Hay Festival Arequipa, celebrado no Peru entre os dias 5 e 8 de novembro.

Confira os principais trechos da entrevista:

Capa do livro Un Animal que se Deja Caer — Foto: Lumen

BBC News Mundo: Em princípio, o tema do seu livro é o cabelo — o cabelo como identidade.

Melanie Pérez Arias: Sim, mas eu diria até que o tema é uma anedota, o ponto de partida, quando a protagonista começa, um dia, a perder cabelo sem entender o porquê.

Mas, como centro, existem dois temas chave no livro: a amizade, especificamente a amizade feminina, e a identidade, sobre quem somos quando aquilo que acreditávamos que fôssemos não serve mais, porque caducou ou por algum fato sobrenatural e inexplicável. Não sou mais aquilo, então, o que e quem sou eu?

BBC: Como o livro é de ficção, o que há de você nesta busca, nesta mudança de identidade?

Pérez Arias: É um livro sobre a transformação e a busca de identidade que, na minha opinião, são íntimas. Elas ocorrem primeiramente em um espaço muito minúsculo da alma e, a partir dali, podem se refletir externamente.

Mas, para mim, a transformação da identidade, também como escritora mulher e migrante, é sempre uma busca constante, não apenas de quem sou agora, do lugar que ocupo, mas de quais são as pequenas mudanças que vão ocorrendo.

Na sua essência, na sua personalidade, como você se deixa influenciar pelo entorno, como aquilo em que você acreditava ser uma verdade para você, como uma catedral, desmorona e quanta beleza existe nessa destruição do que você era e na construção do novo.

Somos invadidos por relatos sobre mudanças que são muito duros e apocalípticos. Mas, nestas pequenas transformações em que o tempo passa e você logo descobre que, sim, sou a mesma pessoa, mas não sou a mesma, ali, naquele espaço diferente, acho que existe muita beleza.

E andar acompanhados neste processo de mudança é uma grande sorte. No caso de Miriam, que é a protagonista, ela está acompanhada das suas amigas nesta mudança que ela precisa viver.

E, além disso, parte do que eu queria construir nesta personagem era este acompanhamento que ela se dá a si própria, quando começa a refletir de forma muito íntima sobre o que está acontecendo com seu cabelo, mas também com a sua vida, seus amores, suas afeições, seu relacionamento, seu trabalho e até com seu tempo livre.

BBC: O que acontece quando o corpo falha?

Pérez Arias: O corpo toma decisões que não têm muito a ver com a pessoa e, ao mesmo tempo, têm tudo a ver com ela. Nunca sabemos o que acontece com Miriam, mas, para elas, é uma espécie de traição.

Existe toda uma corrente que fala sobre a somatização e como nossos pensamentos influenciam o corpo.

Mas, na realidade, uma das ideias que eu também queria transmitir neste livro é a do corpo como mistério. Vivemos em uma época em que queremos explicar tudo em excesso e entender absolutamente tudo o que acontece em cada uma das nossas células. Mas muitas coisas estão fora do nosso controle.

Para mim, isso revela muito sobre o quanto preciso deixar ir e o quanto preciso aceitar como destino.

BBC: Outro tema que atravessa todo o livro é o da beleza, a ponto de que a protagonista prefere a morte a ficar sem cabelo. Como mulher, como venezuelana, como você viveu essa pressão estética, que chega a este extremo?

Pérez Arias: Tudo isso foi uma viagem também para mim porque, como mulher venezuelana, minha identidade e minha cultura são totalmente marcadas por estas buscas do protótipo de beleza, desde o Miss Venezuela, que tem um peso muito forte sobre nós, mulheres.

Moro no Peru há anos e voltei à Venezuela em 2023. Boa parte dos comentários tinham relação com a minha transformação física: quantos quilos, a mais ou a menos, eu tinha, como estava o meu cabelo, o quanto eu havia envelhecido.

No livro, eu precisava que minha protagonista fosse uma pessoa totalmente trivial, o que dá na mesma para ela, pois, se fosse uma questão de vida ou morte, eu acabaria matando a personagem no final do livro porque o cabelo caiu e ela não conseguiu resistir.

A lenda de María Lionza e a crença religiosa da santería fazem parte do romance — Foto: Thierry Monasse/Corbis via Getty Images

BBC: Sobre o cabelo, você escreve "não é algo que sangra, mas dói".

Pérez Arias: Eu me perguntava por que o cabelo não seria importante.

Por que o cabelo não seria um motivo para sentir luto? Por que perder o cabelo não seria uma razão para sentir luto?

Não é um braço, não é um membro, você não está, na verdade, em risco de morte. Mas tem a ver com você, com sua própria imagem. E perder esta imagem também é um processo que não deveríamos menosprezar.

E está na nossa cultura. Em toda a cultura latina, mas, na Venezuela, existem até livros falando sobre como a imagem da Miss foi meio que transcendental para nossa cultura, para nossa identidade.

Sempre havíamos sido reconhecidos como o país do petróleo, dos jogadores de baseball e das misses. Não é pouca coisa.

No meu caso, parte do processo de transformação da migração é aceitar isso que é identitário de outro olhar, muito mais crítico, mas também com ternura.

BBC: Você dizia inicialmente que a história é sobre amizade, mas concretamente entre mulheres. E é verdade que os homens aparecem pouco ou são muito secundários...

Pérez Arias: Esta é uma história em que o conjunto das mulheres é protagonista, mas digamos que a decisão não foi tão política quanto eu gostaria de admitir.

Eu não pensei "vou deixar os personagens masculinos relegados".

Muitas decisões na literatura têm a ver com o que a história pede e esta exigia uma fraternidade muito feminina, pois tem a ver com descobertas de temas relacionados com o corpo e com a velhice.

E eu precisava que minha protagonista estivesse bem cuidada com o passar do tempo e bem cuidada com estas amigas.

Como mulheres millennials [nascidas entre 1981 e 1996], estamos também atravessando um processo de descentralização da relação romântica e de retirar os homens do centro de tudo o que significa nossa experiência de vida.

Não digo que seja algo exclusivo dos últimos tempos, mas, neste caso, eu precisava que estas amigas estivessem disponíveis para ela, para que a história avançasse.

Além disso, pessoalmente, a amizade é muito importante e sempre digo que não consigo imaginar onde eu estaria agora não fosse pelas minhas amigas. Não consigo imaginar e isso é assustador.

BBC: Existe um momento em que você coloca na boca de uma personagem: "você não é velha, algum romance deve ter". E, em muitas partes do romance, você indica isso, que a mulher de uma certa idade parece não ter direito ao amor, ao desejo e é até mesmo invisível. Por que você quis transmitir isso?

Pérez Arias: Existe um livro que foi muito importante para mim no processo de produção deste romance, que é Sobre os Ossos dos Mortos [Ed. Todavia, 2019], de Olga Tocarzuk, prêmio Nobel [de 2018].

Neste romance, a protagonista é uma mulher na casa dos 50 anos, que começa a cometer crimes, respaldada pelo anonimato de ser uma mulher de certa idade. Este romance fundiu minha mente.

Ainda estou longe deste momento da vida. Mas, na realidade, o que encontro são muitos relatos de mulheres idosas da minha vida que me dizem que esta é uma boa etapa.

Estamos dominadas pelo relato de que, com a pós-menopausa, tudo ficará mal com seu corpo e também de que, no processo da mulher, você não terá apenas desafios físicos, mas também será apagada da face da Terra.

Mas, no meu romance, a resposta é: 'não, ainda estamos aqui, temos direito a um corpo, ao prazer, à exploração, até a nos transformarmos e sermos pessoas totalmente diferentes, com direito a sermos vistas e lidas'.

Temos ainda muitos desafios como mulheres, mas o futuro para as mulheres idosas, na pós-menopausa, não parece catastrófico, mas sim um futuro libertador.

A escritora venezuelano-peruana Melanie Pérez Arias — Foto: Nolan Rada

BBC: Um dos temas presentes neste romance são os tabus referentes à saúde das mulheres. Nós já superamos isso?

Pérez Arias: Existe um ponto importante. Este romance se passa no final dos anos 1990. Ou seja, Miriam, a protagonista, foi criança perto dos anos 1945-50. É outro momento histórico, em que as mulheres ainda recebiam mais comentários como "não tome banho quando estiver menstruada, não ande de bicicleta, não pode, não pode, não pode".

Sim, acredito que, agora, existem avanços, embora ainda sejam primários, muito vinculados às áreas urbanas. Meninas que crescem nos interiores dos países latino-americanos ficam de fora.

Na própria Venezuela, temos um grande problema com tudo o que se refere à saúde menstrual, a saúde sexual para as meninas não existe e não há informação. Existe uma vulnerabilidade muito grande.

Existe mais acesso à educação, à informação e divulgação online, mas não acredito que os mitos, por exemplo, sobre a menstruação estejam totalmente derrubados. Além disso, o corpo feminino continua sendo um mistério.

BBC: Foi uma decisão política fazer com que seu romance se passasse nos anos 1990 e não posteriormente? [Hugo Chávez chegou ao poder na Venezuela em 1998]

Pérez Arias: Foi uma decisão totalmente política que o romance transcorresse até o final dos anos 1990 e, de fato, quase em 1998. Foi uma decisão narrativa porque, se Miriam estivesse no presente, ela entraria no ChatGPT ou no Google, ficaria sabendo por que o cabelo cai e o romance teria 30 páginas.

Mas também foi algo absolutamente consciente e político o fato de deixar de fora tudo o que tivesse relação com a história recente da Venezuela e com o chavismo. Eu não queria que eles aparecessem em nenhum momento, pois já são onipresentes demais na minha história e na história do país para também aparecerem no meu primeiro romance.

BBC: Para quem conhece a Venezuela, o romance é um viagem por muitas paisagens do país, cujos nomes você não menciona, mas que estão ali. Como foi escrever sobre esses lugares estando em Lima, no Peru?

Pérez Arias: O caso é que terminei o romance na Venezuela. Mas, antes, foi interessante escrever sobre um território geográfico sem estar nele e ainda sem mencioná-lo, pois eu não queria que houvesse muitos sinais e nomes.

A saudade nos traz a necessidade de encher de nomes, de renomear, de enfeitar as coisas. A saudade nos traz a necessidade de indicar nossos espaços e recuperar nossa linguagem. Mas eu queria que o romance fosse um espaço mais aberto porque esta é uma história muito mais universal. Eu queria que pessoas de todo o mundo pudessem viajar para esse lugar onde estão as protagonistas.

BBC: Miriam recorre à ciência, recorre às amigas, recorre à santería ...

Pérez Arias: A santería [prática que mescla tradições católicas e o culto aos orixás] está por toda parte. A cultura iorubá, a santería , a religião iorubá está em toda parte. Não só na Venezuela, e faz parte do nosso legado, como países colonizados e como países independentes.

Além disso, recebemos toda a cultura africana através da escravidão. Negá-la ou tentar encobri-la apenas com a religião católica, ou até satanizá-la, é uma pressão existente na cultura caribenha. Mas estas manifestações sempre conseguem encontrar uma forma de encontrar seu curso.

Evidentemente, tudo tem um lado luminoso e um lado obscuro. Mas o que me interessava era que minhas personagens estivessem em contato com o lado luminoso desta religião e desta cultura, até porque a ciência abandona minha protagonista. Ela não entende por que o cabelo dela cai, não consegue respostas.O que faço?

Todas nós passamos, em algum momento, pela ideia de "e se eu ler as cartas? E se lançar os búzios? E se perguntar ao horóscopo?" Porque é normal, é também muito próprio da nossa cultura. E eu queria que fosse retratado de forma muito respeitosa, com muita beleza, do ponto de vista luminoso, porque, obviamente, é também assim que eu vivenciei quando morava na Venezuela. Nesta relação com o mágico, com o misterioso, existe algo tão íntimo e tão profundo que eu não queria deixar de fora do romance.

BBC: O que você quer que as pessoas extraiam do seu romance?

Pérez Arias: Que elas se aproximem do romance com a curiosidade de conhecer estas personagens a quem tenho tanto carinho. São personagens que, para mim, são encantadoras, que talvez eu possa prometer que irão ficar com os leitores por um longo tempo. Eu gostaria que elas abordassem o romance com esta curiosidade.

E algo que eu gostaria que elas levassem consigo ao terminarem de ler é que existem coisas que não saberemos explicar sobre o que faz o nosso corpo, mas o meu desejo é que você tenha no caminho a companhia de personagens e pessoas que amam você e tornem as coisas um pouco mais fáceis para você nesta viagem única de nos descobrirmos como seres humanos: falíveis, com corpos que sofrem coisas, porque acontecem coisas com os corpos.

Neste relato, nesta experiência, desejo que você tenha a companhia de amigas e de pessoas que a apoiem e façam você rir.

Parte do que eu queria era que o romance não fosse um drama insuportável sobre mulheres em crise, à beira de um ataque de nervos, mas sim que fosse uma viagem desafiadora, difícil, na qual se pudesse respirar, onde houvesse ar e que esse ar fosse também marcado pelo humor, pela vontade de rir das nossas tragédias, que é o que há de mais latino-americano.

articles.title: Festival de teatro gratuito em Boa Vista celebra 25 anos da Criart | G1
articles.standfirst: Público poderá assistir as peças 'Cordel do Amor Sem Fim', 'Tiquim' e 'A Formiga Fofoqueira'. Programação celebra os 25 anos da companhia Criart Teatral.
articles.summary: Festival de teatro gratuito em Boa Vista celebra os 25 anos da Criart com drama, palhaçaria e mostra histórica no Teatro Municipal neste sábado e domingo.
articles.body:
Peças da da companhia Criart Teatral, fundada em 2021 em Roraima — Foto: Criart Teatral/Divulgação

A companhia de teatro Criart apresenta três espetáculos gratuitos neste sábado (21) e domingo (22), no Teatro Municipal de Boa Vista . A programação celebra os 25 anos do grupo em Roraima . Os ingressos podem ser retirados na bilheteria uma hora antes de cada sessão.

Com o tema, " Criart 25 Anos: Nossa História em Cena ", o festival tem apresentações que incluem drama, palhaçaria — linguagem teatral que usa humor, improvisação e técnicas de palhaço para contar histórias, e uma montagem infantil. Veja a programação:

" Cordel do Amor Sem Fim " – neste sábado (21), às 20h. O drama contemporâneo acompanha as irmãs Carminha, Madalena e Tereza em uma trama de paixões, desejos e escolhas que também envolvem conflitos familiares. A classificação é para maiores de 14 anos.

" Tiquim " – neste domingo (22), às 16h. A montagem aposta na palhaçaria para contar as confusões de Mulica, Dona Jura, Caramela, Trambolho e Sidó após receberem um convite misterioso.

" A Formiga Fofoqueira " – neste domingo (22), às 19h. A peça apresenta uma história ambientada no campo, com fantasia, realidade e personagens inusitados.

A programação começou nesta sexta-feira (20), com “Clarices”. Inspirada na obra de Clarice Lispector, a montagem combina poesia e performance para abordar identidade, existência e as múltiplas experiências de ser mulher. A sessão ocorre no Teatro Escola.

Além das apresentações, o festival oferece ao público a oportunidade de conhecer um pouco mais da história do Criart Teatral desde a fundação,em 2001. A exposição “ Criart Teatral – 25 Anos ” reúne lembranças de diferentes momentos da trajetória do grupo, com fotografias, lambe-lambe, miniaturas de cenários, peças interativas, troféus e outros objetos.

A mostra fica aberta à visitação até este domingo, no hall do Teatro Escola, no Teatro Municipal.

Fundado pela atriz e diretora Kaline Barroso, em 2001, o Criart construiu uma trajetória dedicada à produção artística, à formação e à democratização do acesso à cultura. Ao longo de 25 anos, desenvolveu espetáculos para diferentes públicos, participou de festivais regionais e nacionais e conquistou reconhecimentos, entre eles o Prêmio Myriam Muniz de Teatro e premiações no Festival de Teatro da Amazônia (Fetam).

Como parte da programação de aniversário, a companhia homenageou pessoas que ajudaram a construir a trajetória do grupo dentro e fora dos palcos, com reconhecimento a artistas, profissionais dos bastidores, parceiros e representantes de instituições culturais.

Foram homenageados Graça Paula, responsável pela confecção de figurinos, e Baronso Lucena, que há anos contribui com a iluminação dos espetáculos. Também receberam reconhecimento Fábio Cavalcante, pela contribuição jornalística e divulgação do trabalho do grupo, e as preparadoras corporal e vocal Alexsandra Paz e Nathália Lago.

A homenagem também contemplou integrantes de grupos parceiros, como Arteatro e Locombia, além de representantes do poder público e de instituições culturais.

Leia outras notícias do estado no g1 Roraima .

articles.title: Festival do Beiradão: Manaus recebe shows gratuitos até 27 de novembro | G1
articles.standfirst: Shows gratuitos iniciam às 18h, no Bar Caldeira, com apresentações de Bab Lak do Sax, Nunes Filho e outros artistas. A programação segue até 27 de novembro e celebra a cultura dos beiradeiros.
articles.summary: O Festival do Beiradão inicia programação gratuita no Bar Caldeira com shows de Nunes Filho e Bab Lak do Sax para valorizar a música e a identidade do Amazonas.
articles.body:
Festival celebra 'beiradão', estilo musical tradicional do Amazonas — Foto: Divulgação

A segunda edição do Festival do Beiradão do Amazonas começa nesta segunda-feira (23), em Manaus , com shows gratuitos a partir das 18h, no Bar Caldeira, no Centro Histórico. A abertura marca o início de uma programação que segue até 27 de novembro e reúne artistas para celebrar e valorizar a música e a cultura dos beiradeiros.

A programação de lançamento contará com apresentações de Bab Lak do Sax, Kaiza Marques, Nunes Filho, Nayan da Guitarra, Os Kuximawara, Los Matrinxãs, Marcelo Nakamura e Maestro Janjão.

O festival busca fortalecer o beiradão como parte da identidade cultural do Amazonas e ampliar o debate sobre o reconhecimento dessa manifestação como patrimônio cultural.

A iniciativa também pretende destacar a importância de preservar a tradição e criar políticas públicas para manter essa expressão cultural. A segunda edição ainda promove o encontro entre diferentes gerações de artistas, com atividades ligadas à cultura, à economia criativa e à formação.

articles.title: My Hero Academia returns to Crunchyroll with a 105-minute movie featuring Deku, Bakugo and Todoroki
articles.summary: Fans of My Hero Academia had another reason to return to the world of professional heroes and dangerous villains.
articles.body: Fans of My Hero Academia had another reason to return to the world of professional heroes and dangerous villains. The franchise's third theatrical film, World Heroes’ Mission, arrived on Crunchyroll on November 20, 2026, giving viewers another chance to follow Izuku Midoriya, Katsuki Bakugo and Shoto Todoroki beyond their usual school battles. The 105-minute film offered a global threat, a race against time and a new character who played an important role in Deku's journey.My Hero Academia: World Heroes’ Mission brings Deku back to CrunchyrollOriginally released in Japan on August 6, 2021, World Heroes’ Mission was directed by Kenji Nagasaki and produced by Studio BONES. Creator Kohei Horikoshi served as chief supervisor and handled character design, keeping the film connected to the wider anime universe.The story unfolded during the Endeavor Agency arc, but moved the young heroes far beyond the familiar surroundings of U.A. High School. This time, they faced Humarise, an organisation convinced that people with Quirks posed a threat to humanity's future.Led by Flect Turn, the group planned to spread deadly toxins through bombs placed in locations around the world. The threat forced Pro Heroes and students into an international operation to find the devices before they could cause mass destruction.Deku, Bakugo and Todoroki became part of the mission. Their challenge was not simply to defeat another villain. They had to work against a global deadline, with the safety of countless people at stake.The film also introduced Rody Soul, whose connection with Deku added a more personal dimension to the action. Its international setting and focus on teamwork gave the story a different feel from the regular anime episodes.My Hero Academia movie offers Japanese and English versions on CrunchyrollCrunchyroll's November 20 announcement confirmed that the film was available with Japanese audio and English subtitles, as well as an English-dubbed version. However, streaming access may vary by country, so viewers need to check their local catalogue before looking for it.The movie had already made a strong impression in Japanese theatres. It reportedly earned around 3.18 billion yen at the domestic box office by September 2021. Its music also featured contributions from Asian Kung-Fu Generation, whose songs included the theme track "Empathy" and the insert song "Flowers".For longtime followers, the film offered another look at familiar heroes facing a threat on a much larger scale. New viewers could also explore a major side story from the franchise without following the main series episode by episode.With its return to Crunchyroll, World Heroes’ Mission gave fans another opportunity to revisit Deku and his friends in a high-stakes adventure that expanded the world of My Hero Academia.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Anthony Clark’s Official Cause Of Death Revealed
articles.summary: An official cause of death for Yes, Dear star Anthony Clark has been reported: The comedian, who passed November 10 at 63, died from septic shock, with influ...
articles.body:
An official cause of death for Yes, Dear star Anthony Clark has been reported: The comedian, who passed November 10 at 63, died from septic shock, with influenza A and chronic alcoholism also included as underlying conditions. Acute kidney failure is added as a significant contributing factor.

The details comes from a death certificate obtained by People magazine late yesterday.

The death of Clark, who started his career as a stand-up comedian and later became the star of TV sitcoms Boston Common and Yes, Dear , was announced earlier this month via a social media post from his Yes, Dear co-star and friend Mike O'Malley. Deadline reported at the time that initial reports indicated his death was connected to complications related to pneumonia and the flu. (Clark's age has been variously reported as 62 and 63).

Clark was best known for starring alongside Mike O'Malley, Jean Louisa Kelly and Liza Snyder on the 2000 CBS sitcom Yes, Dear . Created and executive produced by Greg Garcia and Alan Kirschenbaum, the comedy about two couples living under the same roof ran for six seasons.

On hearing the news of Clark's death, Garcia, who also created NBC's My Name I Earl , shared the following thoughts with Deadline:

I've been very lucky to be friends with some of the funniest people in the world, and Anthony Clark had the most insane sense of humor of all of them. The things that would come out of his mouth were so unexpected and hilarious. Over the last two or three years we had reconnected, and I always looked forward to our monthly phone calls where we would catch up and make each other laugh. Recently, he was so full of joy and encouragement when he found out I was trying stand-up comedy for the first time. He enjoyed talking about the art of stand-up, being on the road, and would also offer some great advice. Just a few weeks ago we were laughing hysterically on the phone, trading jokes and telling stories. It's a sad day, and I'll miss him very much. I'm glad he was able to bring a lot of joy and laughter into the world.

articles.title: Ashton Kutcher on track for billionaire status after ignoring wife Mila Kunis' early tech warnings
articles.summary: Ashton Kutcher's Sound Ventures saw its $435 million Anthropic investment grow to $7 billion after the AI company's stock market debut on Nov. 19.
articles.body: Ashton Kutcher is on his way to becoming a billionaire after going against his wife's advice and investing his money in tech. According to Newsweek, the 48-year-old actor's venture capital firm, Sound Ventures, made a $435 million investment in the artificial intelligence company, Anthropic, in 2023, an investment that is now worth $7 billion. Bloomberg reports that the company owns 0.5 percent of Anthropic, which has an estimated IPO valuation of $1.4 trillion. Anthropic went public on the stock exchange on Thursday, Nov. 19. Kutcher co-founded Sound Ventures in 2015 and since then has invested in a number of successful companies. He previously invested in Spotify, Uber and Airbnb with his investment firm, A-Grade Investments, which he co-founded in 2010. WHO IS DARIO AMODEI, THE ANTHROPIC CEO PUSHING INDEPENDENT AI OVERSIGHT? Kutcher has since relinquished his position as partner at Sound Ventures, but has stayed on as a senior advisor. Although the "Two and a Half Men" actor has found success with his investments, his wife, actress Mila Kunis, wasn't always on board with him investing in certain companies. "Early in our dating, two things came up. He was like, ‘Hey, there’s this company, it’s kind of a rideshare,'" she said on "The Late Show with Stephen Colbert Show" in 2021, referencing his investment in Uber. "He’s like, ‘There’s this company, it’s kind of like a cab company, but anyone can drive the cab.’ I was like, ‘That's the worst idea ever.'" The actor decided to convince Kunis by suggesting she try the service herself, an idea which left her "furious." "He is like let me get you this thing, called Uber, let me order it, you can test it out," she said. "And I was like you are going to put me in a car with a stranger. What is wrong with you? Like I was furious at him." He later approached her about investing in Bitcoin, saying he told her, "I gotta explain this thing to you, tell me if I’m crazy," and then told her about "this thing, mining for money, it’s called cryptocurrency." "I was like, ‘Then who is going to make sure it’s safe?’ He was like, ‘That’s the point,'" she said. "He didn’t listen to me...This happens all the time." When speaking with Business Insider in April 2017, Kutcher admitted he initially passed on Uber when the CEO of the company approached him, but then realized "there was a product market fit there" and immediately called the CEO back. He also admitted to having the same feelings about Airbnb, noting his initial thought was, "Who's going to want a stranger sleeping on their couch?" "Oftentimes the foundation of great companies are extraordinarily counterintuitive where the founders have some data nodes that would suggest that the intuition relative to a certain sector is wrong or that there's some fundamental intuition that is wrong," he explained. "And that we when you unveil that fundamental intuition to be wrong, you actually find an entire pasture of green grass that nobody else is building in because there's a fundamental intuition that is that has been an assumption of so many people for so long that they've never actually built into that sector." articles.title: Vishva Hindu Parishad seeks ban on Ranbir Kapoor's 'Ramayana: Part 1', alleging that, 'the film is an attempt to glorify Ravana, historical events have been fabricated'
articles.summary: The controversy surrounding Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer 'Ramayana' has escalated, with the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) demanding that the film's censor
articles.body: The controversy surrounding Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer 'Ramayana' has escalated, with the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) demanding that the film's censor certificate be revoked and its theatrical screenings stopped. VHP International President Alok Kumar accused the makers of distorting elements of the epic and glorifying Ravana, raising objections to the film's portrayal of several characters and events.VHP general secretary Bajrang Lal Bagra also criticised the film for allegedly deviating from Maharishi Valmiki's original Ramayana, claiming that fabricated incidents have been introduced and important characters omitted. In a statement, he alleged that the film attempts to push a political narrative while hurting the religious sentiments of more than one billion devotees of Lord Ram.Speaking about the objections, Alok Kumar said, “We recently watched and reviewed the film ‘Ramayana’, and we have objections to it. Historical events have been distorted and fabricated incidents have been added. This is not merely an attempt to introduce some dramatic elements to make the film entertaining, it also strikes at the very foundational values on which the story of Ram is based. Lord Ram spent 14 years in the forest, meeting people from all sections of society. He lived in the attire of an ascetic and walked barefoot. In an important act of women’s empowerment, he visited Mata Ahilya’s ashram and restored her dignity and respect. Lord Ram and Bharat also referred to Nishadraj as their friend and treated him as an equal. By establishing a bond of friendship with him, they conveyed the message that there is no distinction between touchable and untouchable or between higher and lower castes what matters is the bond of love. Lord Ram’s conduct towards Kevat was also aimed at establishing social harmony. These are essential elements of the Ramayana, but none of them have been depicted in this film."He further alleged that the film presents Ravana in a favourable light and attempts to elevate his character. “From the very beginning, the film portrays Ravana as a liberator of Dalits, the exploited and the deprived, showing him as someone who works for their welfare. This is also an attempt to glorify Ravana," he added.While the Ramayana has traditionally been narrated through the journey of Lord Ram and Sita and the triumph of good over evil, Namit Malhotra's adaptation has also brought Ravana into the spotlight. Played by Yash, the antagonist has been drawing considerable attention from audiences, with many appreciating his portrayal. The growing admiration for the character, however, appears to have become one of the points of contention for the VHP, which has now called for the film to be withdrawn from theatres.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: California's film industry faces uphill battle as Trump steps in and East Coast rivals gain ground
articles.summary: President Trump's "Make Hollywood Great Again" push comes as Hollywood faces declining production, with New Jersey emerging as a "savvy" competitor with uncapped film tax credits.
articles.body: LOS ANGELES — California's entertainment industry continues to face mounting challenges even as Washington steps up efforts to keep film and television production in the United States and President Donald Trump launches a campaign to "Make Hollywood Great Again." Fox News Digital spoke with industry experts to assess the state of Hollywood and examine the mounting pressures on the industry, including intensifying competition from the East Coast. Hollywood runaway production gets White House spotlight "Hollywood doesn’t mean Hollywood anymore. Hollywood is empty," Trump said at a rally in October. "It's not without a lot of truth, unfortunately," entertainment lawyer Jonathan Handel told Fox News Digital. HOLLYWOOD JOBS FLEE OVERSEAS AS CONGRESS SCRAMBLES TO STOP PRODUCTION EXODUS — WITH TRUMP'S BLESSING In recent weeks, President Trump has signaled a new focus on keeping film and television production in the U.S., after years of productions moving overseas in search of lower costs and more lucrative tax incentives. "Hollywood, and so many other places, have been virtually ‘emptied out’ by the Tax Incentives, and much more, given by other Countries. Everyone feels strongly about the Motion Picture and Television Industry — and so do I, and we all want to save it. It was MADE IN AMERICA, and must STAY IN AMERICA," Trump wrote in a post to Truth Social last week. The commander-in-chief said he is working with senators across the aisle, including his longtime political adversary Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., on the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, legislation aimed at bringing the entertainment industry back to the U.S. The push comes as industry experts warn that production is leaving California for competing states and countries at an alarming rate. Shoot days in California are down roughly 40% since 2023, according to data from FilmLA. PELOSI, OMAR JOIN TRUMP AND SCHIFF AS UNLIKELY ALLIANCE PUSHES TO ONSHORE KEY INDUSTRY "It would have been easier to keep this production in Los Angeles than it is to claw it back," Handel said. One significant disadvantage for California is the structure of its tax incentive program, production experts told Fox News Digital. The Golden State’s tax credit is currently capped at $750 million, though California Gov. Gavin Newsom has recently proposed expanding it to at least a $1 billion. Fox News Digital reached out to Gov. Newsom for comment. Meanwhile, states like Georgia offer uncapped credits, while states such as New York and New Jersey offer larger or more flexible incentive structures, allowing productions to access incentives without competing for a limited pool of funding, making them more financially attractive to major studios. "For many, many years, this industry was in California and New York for the most part. And then we saw Canada get into the incentive business. And then, we saw many countries start to build out their own incentive structure. And the truth is, they work," Stagerunner founder and CEO Jason Fisher told Fox News Digital. HOLLYWOOD FEELING MORE HOPEFUL AMID A PUSH FOR FILM TAX CREDITS AND PARAMOUNT STAYING PUT, FILMMAKER SAYS "It's cheaper to go elsewhere," he added. The bipartisan Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, backed by Trump, would create a 20% federal production incentive for films. "There is a movement now and legislation introduced to create a national incentive," Handel said, noting that Ireland and other countries already have national incentives. "That would stack on top of state incentives, whether California, whether Georgia, New Jersey, New York … and is really what's necessary to make production competitive again in California and in the United States," he added. The White House told Fox News Digital in a statement that the Trump administration wants to "Make Hollywood Great Again" and that it is committed to ensuring Hollywood remains a "powerful source of American culture." NETFLIX CHIEF ADMITS TRUMP IS HELPING SHOWBIZ INDUSTRY AS FEDERAL TAX CREDIT BILL AIMS TO FUEL HOLLYWOOD JOBS New Jersey emerges as a rival to California’s moviemaking industry Even with renewed federal attention on domestic production, California faces a separate challenge: competing with other states for film and television projects. A federal incentive could help bring production back from overseas, but it would not eliminate California's disadvantage against states offering more generous tax credits. One of the Golden State's most aggressive competitors is New Jersey, which has attracted major investments from some of Hollywood's biggest players. "They've been a very savvy and very aggressive competitor," Handel said. Netflix, Lionsgate and Skydance are among the entertainment giants investing in New Jersey, where production spending has surged from roughly $67 million to more than $1 billion in less than a decade. Industry experts told Fox News Digital that the state's "aggressive" tax incentives have been a major draw for studios. "They have a 35 percent rebate, perhaps one of the most generous in the country," Fisher told Fox News Digital. "And it also includes above the line. So, it is about as competitive as it gets." NEWSOM DENIES PRESSURING CALIFORNIA AG INTO PARAMOUNT SETTLEMENT AFTER LIBERAL BACKLASH "Netflix is building a studio, Lionsgate’s building a studio, 1888 is another studio being built there," he added. "There’s a lot of infrastructure." Fisher also pointed to California's lengthy and complicated application process as a factor discouraging studios from filming in the state. "Filling out the application process in California, it is a gigantic hassle," said the former production executive. "And it's an application. You aren't guaranteed acceptance." He said states with uncapped tax incentives offer producers greater certainty when planning projects, making them more attractive for producers. "When there's no cap, you don't have to fill out an application and be accepted. They're not choosing which projects to give the incentive to … and that makes it a lot easier for producers," he added. ROB RIGGLE SAYS HOLLYWOOD WORK IS DISAPPEARING FROM LA: 'IT'S THE EXCEPTION NOW' Handel said California's limited pool of tax credits makes it increasingly difficult for the state to compete with jurisdictions offering productions more generous, uncapped incentives. "When you're competing against … uncapped incentives in New Jersey, Georgia, and the European countries, it's not enough," the entertainment lawyer said. As other states offered increasingly competitive incentives, studios began investing in permanent production infrastructure in New Jersey, New Mexico, Texas and Georgia, further shifting the industry's center of gravity away from California. "As we saw those incentive programs grow, then we saw infrastructure build out. We saw companies building sound stages, we saw a local crew workforce training happening," Fisher told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "And so, once you've got vendors, local crew, sound stages and a competitive incentive, there's no reason to stay here [in California] anymore," he added.

articles.body: Ty Pennington has built and maintained a successful career with his extreme home makeovers, but there's one renovation trend he believes homeowners are taking a little too far these days. "I would probably say the island with three dishwashers," the veteran HGTV star, 62, said when asked about renovation trends that go overboard. "It's maybe a little excessive. This is coming from somebody who was a personal dishwasher for many years of my life." JOANNA GAINES REVEALS WHY SHE AND CHIP WALKED AWAY FROM 'FIXER UPPER' AT THE HEIGHT OF ITS SUCCESS "There is a point that you almost get too big," he continued. "Is there an island that's almost the size of a small court? Possible. So I think sometimes we may be sort of outgrowing things. We may be just going too big. While Pennington advocates for dialing back the scale, he still acknowledges that kitchens and bathrooms remain the smartest investments for homeowners looking to build equity. "The most expensive are the kitchens and the bathrooms, but I do think they're kind of necessary if you plan on selling, because that's what people look at first," he explained. articles.title: Ranking the top six 'Grand Theft Auto VI' in-game radio stations, from V-Rock to Vice City FM
articles.summary: "Grand Theft Auto VI" packs 22 radio stations, and this ranking crowns V-Rock No. 1, with Emotion 98.3 yacht rock and Vice City FM's 80s vibes close behind.
articles.body: If you’ve played even five minutes of "Grand Theft Auto VI" since its release, you know just how immersive this video game is. There are miles of swamps and beaches to explore, realistic NPC interactions and I even made an entire article about how realistic the game’s version of South Florida is when compared to its real-life counterpart. But one mechanic that has been included in the new game that’s been around since the early days of the series are the radio stations, and "GTA VI" has the most diverse radio dial yet. REDDIT'S BIRDING COMMUNITY GOES WILD AS UNIQUE 'GRAND THEFT AUTO 6' FEATURE COMES TO LIGHT All in all, there are 22 unique radio stations in the game, and each of them offers a different soundtrack to your wheeling and stealing as you traverse through Leonida. Being a huge fan of the series and music in general, I thought it would be fun to rank my six favorite "GTA VI" radio stations. This wasn’t easy, as there are a ton of great stations to choose from, and I even had to omit a few that I really liked (sorry, Back Country Radio). With that said, let’s rank the best that "GTA VI" has to offer in the form of music. 6. Flash FM By virtue of hitting the "quantity over quality" metrics, Flash FM sneaks its way onto the list at number six. Don't get me wrong, there are heaps of awful songs on this station, but there are some gems in there too. Echosmith, Foster The People, Gwen Stefani, and MGMT will have Millennials bobbing their heads as they commit vehicular homicide (in the game), and newcomers like Ella Langley and Addison Rae offer enough to be passable cruising songs when there's nothing else on. Flash FM isn't the stalwart it was back in the '80s for "Grand Theft Auto: Vice City," but there is enough fun to be had here for this station to find its way into the rotation. 5. Dirty South Classics This one might be a bit of a nostalgia pick for me, but I don't care. Having grown up and gone to high school in South Florida, a lot of the songs on this station were popular right around the time my life was centered around algebra tests and getting rejected by chicks, so playing a game where I can drive around a virtual representation of my hometown while blaring rap songs that were popular 15 years ago is an auto win. If you're into 2000s and 2010s rap, you'll probably have your radio dial locked on Dirty South Classics, with heavy hitters like Lil Wayne, Outkast, Drake, Rick Ross and even Jay Z being well represented here. There is no better feeling than cruising Miami Beach at night listening to "No Lie" by 2Chainz, and it's even cooler when that is also a core memory from your adolescence, minus the cocaine and dead hookers. 4. Vice City FM Now we are getting into rarified air, and Vice City FM begins a string of stations with way more good than bad on them. For those of you who wanted the '80s vibes of "Vice City" to carry over to the new game, you're in luck. MIAMI HEAT UNVEIL VICE CITY COURT FOR 'GRAND THEFT AUTO VI'-THEMED CLASH WITH MILWAUKEE BUCKS Vice City FM is a carryover from the old Playstation 2 game, and the songs you'll find on here will have you thinking you hopped in a DeLorean and landed in 1986. Genesis, Culture Club, Lionel Richie, Billy Idol, The Cars and so much more, you'll be pulling out the AquaNet and legwarmers before your first hour of gameplay. The neon lights of South Florida mesh perfectly with the 80s vibes, and this station makes for a cool nighttime drive soundtrack. For an added bonus, Weird Al Yankovic is one of the in-game DJs, which I thought was a nice touch. 3. The Chamber 106.6 Metal, metal and more metal. That's what you're going to find on The Chamber. While I'm partial to the older stuff, this station has a great mix of classic and newer metal to bridge the generational gap for headbangers. If you're a spiritual Boomer like me, you'll be happy to know acts like Iron Maiden, Judas Priest, Megadeth and, of course, Metallica are littered all over The Chamber. New-school metal disciples will be pleased to hear the likes of Linkin Park, System of a Down, Tool and Sepultura mixed in. Committing virtual crimes is so much more fun when it's set to the brutal riffing and blistering solos of Judas Priest's "Freewheel Burning," but don't just take my word for it, try it yourself. And hey, the station is hosted by Slayer's Tom Araya and Kerry King, so you know it's curated by two legends. 2. Emotion 98.3 Can you name a better combination than the sun-soaked streets of South Florida and some soothing yacht rock? Of course you can't, which is why Emotion 98.3 is sitting in the silver medal spot for "GTA VI" radio stations. Emotion makes its triumphant return as one of the stations featured in "GTA: Vice City," and its setlist will have you looking for the nearest super yacht to steal so that you can enjoy the songs properly. You want soft rock? How does Ace, Chicago, The Doobie Brothers, and Bruce Hornsby sound? And that's just the tip of the iceberg. I spent my entire life being serenaded by these guys while navigating the intracoastal waterways of South Florida, and now I get to do it in a video game. Life sure is sweet sometimes! 1. V-Rock It was never going to be anything else. If you played "GTA: Vice City," you know how legendary this station was. Well, it's back and better than ever, featuring a wide range of classic rock artists that offer the best company on any long drive around Leonida. There are too many bangers to even count, but I'll try: Def Leppard, AC/DC, Aerosmith, Dire Straits, Foreigner, Blue Oyster Cult, Motley Crue, Styx, and ZZ Top, just to name a few. Seriously, I haven't even mentioned another half dozen artists who rank as some of my favorites of all time. Oh, and they have Van Halen, too. In case I needed to nerd out any more than I already am. I also love how they included several Tom Petty songs, given his connection to the Sunshine State. Finally, the station is hosted by Lindsey Buckingham of Fleetwood Mac fame and Michael Freaking McDonald. articles.title: 'Scene' box office collection day 16 vs 'Mookuthi Amman 2': Suriya's film crosses Rs 262 cr worldwide; Saturday earnings jump 75.3%; Nayanthara's movie grosses Rs 24.80 cr
articles.summary: Suriya's 'Scene', directed by Jithu Madhavan, recorded an improvement in its box office performance on Saturday, November 21.
articles.body: Suriya's 'Scene', directed by Jithu Madhavan, recorded an improvement in its box office performance on Saturday, November 21. The movie collected Rs 1.35 cr in India net earnings on Day 16, with 731 shows across its Tamil and Telugu versions. The Tamil version accounted for Rs 1.10 cr from 499 shows, while the Telugu version added Rs 25 lakh through 232 shows.According to Sacnilk reports, the latest day's collection was 75.3% higher than Friday's Rs 77 lakh. The film's cumulative India net collection has now reached Rs 149.07 cr, while its domestic gross stands at Rs 173.17 cr. Its highest single-day collection remains the Rs 23.65 cr recorded on Day 3.The overseas market added Rs 25 lakh on Saturday, taking the cumulative overseas gross to Rs 89.25 cr. This pushed the worldwide gross to Rs 262.42 cr after 16 days in theatres. The movie is now progressing towards the Rs 300 cr worldwide milestone.'Scene' records a Saturday recovery after second-week declineThe film's weekly figures show a considerable slowdown after its opening week. Between Days 1 and 7, 'Scene' earned Rs 111.70 cr in India net collections and Rs 129.75 cr in gross collections.The second week, covering Days 8 to 14, brought in Rs 35.25 cr net and Rs 40.95 cr gross. This represented a 68.4% decline from the first week's business. During the third week, the movie collected Rs 2.12 cr net and Rs 2.47 cr gross across Days 15 and 16.The film has recorded 68,513 shows during its 16-day theatrical run. Saturday saw an estimated 102,492 tickets sold, taking the cumulative ticket sales to 11,333,480.Tamil version accounts for nearly 80% of India net collectionThe Tamil version continues to lead the domestic box office contribution. It has earned Rs 119.12 cr, accounting for 79.9% of the total India net collection. The Telugu version has contributed Rs 29.95 cr, making up the remaining 20.1%.The difference was also visible in Saturday's occupancy figures. The Tamil version recorded 54% occupancy across 499 shows, while the Telugu version registered 31% from 232 shows. The gap between them stood at 23 percentage points.The Tamil 2D version registered an overall occupancy of 64.62% on Day 16. Its morning shows recorded 35.31%, while afternoon and evening screenings registered 56.38% and 46.38%, respectively. Night shows saw the highest occupancy at 68%.The Telugu 2D version reported an overall occupancy of 24.43%. Morning shows registered 21.30%, followed by 20.40% in the afternoon. Evening occupancy stood at 18.80%, while night screenings recorded 22.90%.The film's domestic gross accounts for 66% of its worldwide earnings, with overseas markets contributing the remaining 34%. The international business has therefore remained an important part of its overall box office performance.'Mookuthi Amman 2' earns Rs 24.80 cr worldwideMeanwhile, Nayanthara's 'Mookuthi Amman 2' has recorded a worldwide gross of Rs 24.80 cr after 16 days in theatres. The figures, reported through November 21, 2026, include an India net collection of Rs 21.52 cr. Its India gross also stands at Rs 24.80 cr, while no overseas collection has been reported.The movie earned Rs 2 lakh on Day 16, registering a 100% increase over its previous day's collection. Its worldwide total remains considerably lower than the figure achieved by 'Scene' over the same 16-day period. articles.summary: Amal Neerad's 'Bachelor Party D'eux', starring Naslen, Soubin Shahir, Sreenath Bhasi, Tovino Thomas and Kunchacko Boban, continued to experience a
articles.body: Amal Neerad's 'Bachelor Party D'eux', starring Naslen, Soubin Shahir, Sreenath Bhasi, Tovino Thomas and Kunchacko Boban, continued to experience a slowdown at the box office on Saturday. The Malayalam film collected Rs 37 lakh net in India on its third day, registering a 35.1% decline from Friday. Its three-day domestic earnings have reached Rs 3.49 cr net, with the gross collection standing at Rs 4.11 cr. The film's Saturday performance also marked a considerable drop from its opening-day business. It recorded an average of approximately Rs 4,579 per show across its theatrical screenings.'Bachelor Party D'eux' records another decline on SaturdayAccording to Sacnilk, the film opened with a promising performance on Thursday but could not maintain the same momentum over the following two days. Its Friday earnings dropped by 77.6% compared with the opening day. Saturday brought a further decline, although the rate of fall was less severe than the previous day's.The film collected Rs 37 lakh net from 808 shows on Saturday. Its overall occupancy for the day stood at 14%, while the cumulative footfall reached 2,51,690. The latest figures indicate that the movie is yet to regain the momentum witnessed during its opening-day run.The Malayalam version continues to account for almost the entire domestic box-office business of 'Bachelor Party D'eux'. It has contributed Rs 3.44 cr, representing 98.6% of the film's India net collections. The Telugu version has added Rs 5 lakh, accounting for the remaining 1.4%.The Malayalam 2D version recorded an overall occupancy of 13.59% on Saturday. Night screenings registered the highest occupancy at 21%, followed by evening shows at 12.5%. Afternoon screenings recorded 10.25%, while morning shows reported 5.17%. The figures indicate that the movie attracted a relatively better audience during the later screenings.Night shows lead Saturday occupancyDespite the overall decline in collections, night shows performed better than the other time slots. Their occupancy was considerably higher than the morning and afternoon figures. However, the overall response remained modest, with the film recording an average occupancy below 15% across its Saturday screenings.'Bougainvillea' had a stronger third-day performanceAmal Neerad's previous directorial venture, 'Bougainvillea', performed considerably better at the same stage of its theatrical run. According to Sacnilk, the film earned Rs 2.85 cr net and Rs 3.31 cr gross in India on its third day, Saturday, October 19, 2024. Its collections increased by 26.7% compared with the second day, when it had earned Rs 2.25 cr net.'Bougainvillea' had accumulated Rs 8.40 cr in India net collections during its opening three days. Its third-day performance included 1,621 shows and an overall occupancy of 37%.'Bachelor Party D'eux' is presented as a spiritual successor to Amal Neerad's 2012 Malayalam film 'Bachelor Party'. The new movie revisits the world of friendship, chaos and irreverent humour through a fresh storyline. articles.title: '32 years ago he whispered softly': Harshvardhan Rane shares 22-year-old picture with John Abraham; gets fans curious about 'Force 3'
articles.summary: Actor Harshvardhan Rane recently shared a series of photographs offering fans a glimpse into different phases of his life.
articles.body: Actor Harshvardhan Rane recently shared a series of photographs offering fans a glimpse into different phases of his life. One picture, taken 22 years ago, features him alongside John Abraham, his co-star in the upcoming movie 'Force 3'. The throwback image has drawn attention because of Harshvardhan's noticeably different appearance at the time.The actor posted the photograph as part of an Instagram album that also featured a picture of his latest tattoo. The new ink carries the words, "You will get it slowly". Harshvardhan shared a close-up of the tattoo on Saturday and accompanied it with a message about trusting one's instincts.He wrote, "32 years ago he whispered softly...Trust in the small voice, You will get it slowly. (sic)." The post also included a more recent photograph, taken two days earlier, in which Harshvardhan can be seen walking along a beach. A childhood picture from 32 years ago completed the collection.Harshvardhan Rane shares throwback picture with John AbrahamThe photograph with John Abraham dates back 22 years and shows the actors together long before their upcoming collaboration. Harshvardhan's appearance in the old picture has particularly caught the attention of followers. The two actors will now be seen together in 'Force 3', the third instalment of the popular action franchise. The film also stars Tanya Maniktala and is directed by Bhav Dhulia.'Force 3' gets a March 2027 release date'Force 3' makers have scheduled its theatrical release for March 19, 2027. Further details about the film's storyline and the characters played by the other cast members have not been mentioned in the available announcement. In another recent development, Harshvardhan Rane received a Range Rover as a gift from producer Deepak Mukut. The actor responded by making a request for a sequel to their 2016 romantic drama 'Sanam Teri Kasam'. He wants Deepak Mukut to approve the project, which has remained a subject of interest among the film's fans.Harshvardhan also recalled his earlier visit to the producer's office with fans, when they had sought a theatrical re-release of the movie. He said he planned to return with them on his birthday next month, this time to request approval for the sequel.He wrote, "Deepak Sir I've been part of many promises, but you stand apart. You're truly a man of your word. Sir, just as I stood outside your office (Soham Rockstar Entertainment) last year, alongside fans requesting the re-release of Sanam Teri Kasam, I'll be back at your doorstep with them on my birthday next month."He added, "This time, with one request: your approval for Sanam Teri Kasam 2. Script and Director of your choice! Will you grant me and the fans this birthday wish, sir? (guys lets start tagging @sohamrockstrent)," he added.Meanwhile, his last theatrical release was 'Ek Deewane Ki Deewaniyat', which arrived in October 2025.
